cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel the prophet again, and this time it's aimed at one man: Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. God tells Ezekiel to set his face against Gog and prophesy against him. And the message opens with God saying, Behold, I am against you, O Gog.
God says He will turn Gog around, put hooks in his jaws, and bring him out. Friend, that's not a road trip. That's getting TOWED.

cards.question: God says He'll bring Gog out with all his ___.

cards.text: Horses, horsemen in full armor, shields and swords, plus Persia, Cush, Put, Gomer and Beth-togarmah from the far north. The biggest crowd I ever saw in my junk drawer was a pile of rubber bands, and this guy shows up with NATIONS.

cards.question: God tells Gog to get ready and prepare himself and all the company gathered around him.

cards.text: But this won't happen soon. God says after a long time Gog will be summoned, and in the latter years he'll enter a land that has recovered from war, on the mountains of Israel, which had long been desolate.

cards.question: By the latter years, who lives in that land on the mountains of Israel?
When Gog enters the land in the latter years, its people are still living as captives in other nations.

cards.text: By then the people are home, and all of them dwell securely. Then Gog and all his troops will go up, advancing like a thunderstorm, like a cloud covering the land.

cards.question: On that day, God says thoughts will arise in Gog's mind. What will Gog devise?

cards.text: Then Gog says his plan out loud. He'll come against a quiet people who dwell securely.

cards.question: What does Gog say about the land of these quiet people?

answers.text: They live without walls or gates
Their land still lies in ruins

cards.question: Gog goes up against this quiet land to seize its spoil and carry off its plunder.

cards.text: Gog isn't the only one watching. Sheba and Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish see the whole thing, and they have questions.

cards.question: Sheba, Dedan and the merchants of Tarshish ask Gog if he has come to carry away ___.

cards.text: Then God has Ezekiel speak to Gog again: "On that day when My people Israel are dwelling securely, will you not take notice of this?" Oh, Gog is going to notice, friend.

cards.question: Gog comes against Israel out of the far south.

cards.text: A mighty horde, all riding horses, advancing like a cloud covering the land. Then God makes something clear: in the latter days, He is the One bringing Gog against His land.

cards.question: Why does God say He will bring Gog against His land?

answers.text: So the nations may know Him
So Gog's own people are punished
So Israel's army can be tested

cards.text: Then God asks Gog a question: is he the one God has spoken of in former days?

cards.question: God says He spoke of Gog in former days through His servants, the ___ of Israel.

cards.text: I bet Gog figured this whole invasion was his own idea. Now God speaks of the day Gog comes against the land of Israel.

cards.question: When Gog comes against the land of Israel, God says His wrath will flare up.

cards.text: In His zeal and fiery rage, God proclaims what will happen in the land of Israel on that day.

cards.question: God says on that day there will be a great ___ in the land of Israel.
On that day, who does God say will tremble at His presence?

cards.text: God says the mountains will be thrown down, the cliffs will collapse, and every wall will fall to the ground.

cards.question: God summons a sword against Gog on all His mountains. What does God say every man's sword will be against?

cards.text: God says He'll judge Gog with plague and bloodshed, and pour out torrents of rain, hailstones, fire and sulfur on him, his troops and the many nations with him.

cards.question: When it's all over, God says many nations will know that He is the LORD.

cards.text: God says He will magnify and sanctify Himself and reveal Himself in the sight of many nations. Hold that thought, friend, because God has more to say about Gog.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the retelling, "Friend, that's not a road trip," and "That's getting TOWED." It needs to be reduced to two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Verse 17 asks whether Gog is the one of whom God previously spoke; it does not explicitly settle that identification. This card turns the question into the assertion that God spoke of Gog in former days. The question should preserve the wording of the setup, such as asking whether Gog is the one God spoke of through His servants, the prophets of Israel.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The preceding story card says only that God proclaims what will happen in His zeal and fiery rage. Earthquake, drought, and famine are all plausible judgments, so the baker has no basis for reasoning to "earthquake" and can only guess the unseen wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
